papers.title: Geometry-Conditioned Hyperalignment for Generalizable EEG Decoding Across Datasets and Paradigms
papers.summary: Introduces hTSMNet, combining geometry-conditioned hyperalignment, which maps any electrode montage onto fixed scalp anchors using coordinates alone, with an SPD manifold backbone for zero-shot cross-subject and cross-dataset EEG decoding. On a leave-one-dataset-out motor-imagery benchmark across three datasets (172 subjects), it matched the strongest zero-shot comparator and achieved the highest accuracy on every dataset after minimal classifier-only calibration; the frozen model also transferred to mental workload and SSVEP but not stimulus-locked ERP, indicating generalization of band-limited oscillatory representations rather than named tasks.

papers.title: LBSNet: Lightweight Brain State Modeling via Learnable Spectral Prototypes for EEG-Based Fatigue Detection
papers.summary: Proposes LBSNet, a lightweight EEG fatigue-detection network that matches normalized window-level spectral descriptors to learnable spectral prototypes, whose assignments and importance weight temporal power aggregation. In subject-independent tests on SEED-VIG and SADT it outperformed seven baselines at low computational cost, and learned prototypes showed gradual redistribution of relative cross-band spectral states with increasing fatigue.

papers.title: BioLT: Streaming Biosignal Modeling
papers.summary: Introduces BioLT, a streaming decoder-only framework that converts window-level biosignal feature extractors or foundation models into long-context streaming models via discontinuity-aware encoding of inter-window elapsed time and a compressed memory bank. Across 21 dataset-feature settings on four datasets, BioLT achieved the highest detection AUROC in 15 and highest 20-minute forecasting AUROC in 13 settings.

papers.title: Using wearable EEG to examine age trends in sleep macro- and micro-architecture across adolescence
papers.summary: Tested whether the Dreem3 wearable EEG headband can replicate established age-related trends in sleep physiology in 100 typically developing youth aged 9-26 across 3-4 nights of at-home recording. The device reproduced some expected trends, including rising NREM stage 2% and declining N3%, time in bed, and NREM delta and theta power with age, while several other associations did not reach significance.

papers.title: Automated intracranial spike analysis across sleep-wake states localizes the seizure onset zone in drug-resistant epilepsy.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Used FDA-cleared automated sleep staging and IED detection on 48-72 h of intracranial EEG from 17 EPILEPSIAE and 10 pediatric patients to test a novel amplitude- and channel-consistency-aware IED activity metric for seizure-onset zone localization across sleep-wake states. IED activity was higher in SOZ channels in every state, with N2 sleep giving the highest AUROC (0.69 EPILEPSIAE; 0.77 ACH) and only modest, non-significant state differences.

papers.title: A human-like EEG signature of cognitive control in the domestic dog.
papers.summary: Compared short (~30 s) EEG recordings during passive wakefulness versus a delayed gratification challenge in fourteen family dogs (226 recordings) to probe neural correlates of cognitive control. The test condition showed increased 4-8 Hz activity that was more pronounced over the frontal midline, resembling human cognitive theta, together with reduced broadband power and a flattened spectrum.

papers.title: Macroscale dynamics of EEG microstates constitute the periodic and aperiodic features of the neural power spectrum
papers.summary: Used orthogonal subspace projection to remove spatial projections of distinct EEG microstate configurations from high-density scalp recordings and modeled cortical generators, then spectrally parameterized the residual power. Removing these projections attenuated alpha and theta rhythms and the aperiodic 1/f background in configuration-specific ways, and microstate duration and temporal persistence correlated strongly with periodic alpha, theta, and 1/f features, supporting microstate dynamics as the time-domain source of periodic and aperiodic spectra.

papers.title: Advanced Two-Stage Authentication with EEG: Inter-Subject P300 ERP Classification Using EEGNet for User Recognition.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Proposes a two-stage EEG authentication framework combining multi-class user identification and binary authentication using P300 ERP features and EEGNet, with a preprocessing pipeline of filtering, epoch rejection, cropping, and downsampling. Across 16 participants and three sessions, the system reached up to 95% precision and a mean accuracy of 96.10% for identification and authentication.

papers.title: CABrain: A Correlation-Aware Brain Foundation Model for EEG Decoding
papers.summary: Introduced CABrain, an EEG foundation model pretraining approach using GCN-based conditional positional encoding to model inter-channel correlations and an adaptive masking strategy to modulate reconstruction difficulty. Both strategies, individually and combined, achieved state-of-the-art or competitive performance across ten benchmark EEG decoding datasets.

papers.title: MambaPD: Bidirectional Selective State Space Model for Parkinson's Disease Detection from Resting-State EEG
papers.summary: Proposed MambaPD, a bidirectional selective state space model for resting-state EEG detection of Parkinson's disease, benchmarked against TCN, BiLSTM-attention, EEGNet and patch Transformer baselines with subject-independent cross-validation. MambaPD reached 0.714 accuracy on UNM (comparable to Transformer 0.715 and TCN 0.708) and 0.631 on SanDiego, with performance differences minor relative to fold variability.

papers.title: Scalp EEG seizure warning in children under a pre-specified, locked evaluation: confound audit, structured chance levels and a negative result
papers.summary: Evaluated scalp EEG seizure warning in 21 monitored children under a pre-specified, locked protocol, finding the initial method (44% of seizures, 0.48 false alarms/hour) no better than chance. A redesigned state-conditioned scheme achieved 33% detection during cross-validation but failed to exceed structured chance in two external validation cohorts (19% detection at 0.60 false alarms/hour versus 26% chance), a negative result.

papers.title: Exploring Data Augmentation for Stroke Severity Prediction: How Generative AI Enhances EEG Signal Classification
papers.summary: Evaluated traditional oversampling (SMOTE, ADASYN) and generative augmentation (WGAN, WGAN-GP) within a hybrid pipeline of preprocessing, statistical and frequency-domain feature extraction, feature selection, and classifiers for EEG-based stroke severity prediction in 50 patients. The combination of SelectKBest, SVM, and WGAN-GP augmentation achieved the highest accuracy at 72%, outperforming the other methods.

papers.title: Feasibility of Vibrotactile P50 Sensory-Gating Assessment Using Portable EEG
papers.summary: Evaluated feasibility of a portable vibrotactile P50 sensory-gating paradigm against auditory gating in 15 healthy adults using 32-channel portable EEG. Vibrotactile stimulation elicited time-locked P50 responses with S2 attenuation, and mean S2/S1 ratios did not differ significantly between auditory (0.521) and vibrotactile (0.524) conditions.

papers.title: Patient-level EEG seizure classification with AHCNet: Hybrid CNN and handcrafted feature fusion.
papers.summary: Developed AHCNet, a hybrid model fusing a multiscale 1D CNN with handcrafted spectro-temporal and inter-channel spatial features for patient-level EEG seizure classification in 198 patients. Feature fusion and stacking reached accuracies of 78.3% and 78.8%, segment-level validation inflated accuracy by 20-23 points, metadata alone reached 72.2%, and deferring the 20% least-confident patients raised accuracy to 84.8%.

papers.title: Serial Amplitude-Integrated Electroencephalography and the Burdjalov Score in Preterm Infants: A Prospective Longitudinal Bedside Study in the Neonatal Care Unit.
papers.summary: Prospectively assessed interobserver reproducibility of the Burdjalov score and longitudinal electrocortical maturation via serial two-channel amplitude-integrated EEG in 48 preterm infants (125 recordings) plus 29 term references. Total-score agreement was excellent (ICC 0.98) and scores rose continuously with corrected gestational age, approaching maximal values around 37 weeks and matching term infants, with no difference in time to maturity across gestational-age strata.

papers.title: A Breathable Nanomesh-Textile Electrode Interface for Integrated Multimodal Monitoring.
papers.summary: Introduced a duo-electrode interface for wearable electrophysiology that separates skin contact (electrospun nanomesh tattoo electrode) from electronic interconnection (compressible conductive taffeta-foam textile electrode in a garment). Integrated into a bodysuit and eyemask for multimodal ECG, EMG, EOG, and body-position monitoring, the system maintained reliable signals under motion and muscle activation, comparable to or better than commercial hydrogel electrodes.

papers.title: BiXCA-DualFormer: A time-frequency fusion model for epileptic seizure prediction.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers. Part H, Journal of engineering in medicine
papers.summary: Proposes BiXCA-DualFormer, a dual-branch time-frequency fusion model that processes raw EEG and short-time Fourier representations through separate temporal and spectral branches with bidirectional cross-attention, a Transformer encoder, and learnable query pooling for seizure prediction. On CHB-MIT it achieved 95.29% accuracy, 96.40% sensitivity, 95.05% specificity, and a 0.0495 false positive rate.

papers.title: Capturing continuous spectrotemporal pupil--brain coupling with simultaneous wearable EEG/Eye tracking
papers.summary: Used wearable mobile EEG (MUSE) and eye tracking (Tobii Pro Glasses 3) to test whether spectrotemporal and directional pupil-brain coupling is detectable in naturalistic, continuous resting-state recordings with interoceptive attention. Cross-correlation, mutual information, and Granger causality showed frequency-dependent coupling, with lower EEG frequencies (2-12 Hz) preceding pupil dynamics by roughly 764 ms and predominantly EEG-to-pupil directionality, preserved across recording states.

papers.title: Evaluation of Brain Activity in Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder Using Standardized Low Resolution Electromagnetic Tomographic Analyses (sLORETA).
papers.summary: Evaluated Default Mode Network activity using archival qEEG and sLORETA in 87 women with PMDD/dysphoric PMS and 70 asymptomatic controls across follicular and luteal phases. PMDD participants showed a significant follicular-to-luteal change in angular gyrus beta2 aberrant-voxel percentage and significantly higher luteal subcallosal-gyrus beta2 mean-Z activity than controls.

papers.title: Distinguishing evidence accumulation from choice confidence in neural signatures of perceptual decision making
papers.summary: Using EEG with 80%-valid predictive cues in a contrast discrimination task, this study dissociated the centro-parietal positivity (CPP) from subjective confidence. Valid cues reduced pre-response CPP amplitude even when confidence was matched, supporting the CPP as an evidence accumulation signal contributing to both decision formation and confidence estimation rather than a direct read-out of confidence.

papers.title: Multimodal EEG-fNIRS complexity analysis can reveal the neurovascular coupling change with aging.
papers.summary: The study used simultaneous EEG-fNIRS with nonlinear entropy analysis in 20 young and 20 older adults across four cognitive tasks, finding age-related task-specific alterations in neural and hemodynamic complexity and their cross-modal relationship, suggesting dynamic reorganization of neurovascular coupling rather than uniform impairment.

papers.title: Multiscale EEG network alterations in adolescents with depressive symptoms: static-dynamic connectivity, topological features, and exploratory scalp-level network hubs.
papers.summary: Using resting-state EEG from 96 adolescents with depressive symptoms and 154 controls, the study identified multiscale network abnormalities: theta-band static hyperconnectivity, reduced dynamic flexibility, and focal topological vulnerability in prefrontal regions, with spatial overlap to neuromodulation hubs.

papers.title: Working memory capacity is linked to directed exploration: behavioral, computational, and electrophysiological evidence
papers.summary: Compared 26 high- and 26 low-working-memory-capacity participants on an adapted Horizon Task with EEG and hierarchical Bayesian reinforcement learning modeling. High-WMC participants showed more directed exploration and less exploitation, with a larger sampling-history discounting parameter omega that statistically mediated the WMC-exploration link (ab = 0.64), and larger frontocentral P2 (180-280 ms) during directed exploration that correlated with the behavioral preference (r = .29).

papers.title: Cortical depth EEG-fMRI at 7T: Experimental setup and analysis pipeline to elucidate generating mechanisms of alpha oscillations.
papers.summary: The authors developed a 7T laminar EEG-fMRI pipeline with deveining to study alpha oscillations, observing negative alpha-BOLD correlations in visual cortex that were weakest in middle cortical depths after vein exclusion, consistent with superficial and deep sources of top-down alpha generation.

papers.title: Beyond Exploration: Heightened Recent Reward Reliance and Midfrontal Sensitivity to Outcome Differences in ADHD
papers.summary: Examined exploratory decision-making in 23 adults with ADHD and 27 controls using a restless four-armed bandit task with EEG across 450 trials. Groups did not differ in exploration rates or performance, but ADHD participants more strongly repeated options after high rewards and switched after low rewards, and showed greater midfrontal sensitivity to unsigned payoff changes in a 280-568 ms feedback-evoked response carried by slow activity below 2 Hz.

papers.title: Simultaneous dynamic spectrophotometric determination of coexisting rare earth elements in acidic chloride media using response-specific multivariate calibration.
papers.summary: The study introduced a dynamic spectrophotometric method with a response-specific multivariate calibration model (RS-MPBLR) for continuous quantification of Nd3+ and Pr3+ in acidic chloride media, achieving R² > 0.97 and detection limits of 0.07 and 0.03 g/L, with stable online predictions.

papers.title: Broadband gamma-band EEG changes during magnetophosphene-inducing 20 Hz magnetic field stimulation.
papers.summary: In 13 healthy volunteers, suprathreshold 20 Hz transcranial alternating magnetic stimulation (50 mT) that induced magnetophosphenes was associated with spatially distributed broadband gamma-band EEG power increases, without a consistent narrowband peak, characterizing the stimulation-perception condition.

papers.title: Sex-related clinical profiles in obstructive sleep apnea: An integrated clinical, sleep study, and drug-induced sleep endoscopy analysis.
papers.summary: In a retrospective DISE-selected cohort of 767 obstructive sleep apnea patients, women were older with more insomnia and mood disorders and more frequent complete collapse resolution with jaw thrust (30.2% vs 18.4%), while men had higher BMI, obstruction at all airway levels, and more frequent surgical recommendations, suggesting an anatomy-driven pattern in men and a functionally modulated profile in women.

papers.title: Evaluating Age-Related Motor System Changes Using Gait as a Functionally Relevant Marker.
papers.summary: In 19,637 walk trials from 5,794 participants in the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging, the authors built a machine-learning model to predict gait age and defined the "gait age gap" as the difference between gait-predicted age and chronological age. Each year of gait age gap above chronological age was associated with a 7% higher annual risk of converting from normal to cognitively impaired (HR 1.07, 95% CI 1.03-1.13), and gait age gap outperformed baseline gait velocity in distinguishing normal from cognitively impaired groups.

papers.title: Effects of Pore Mutations on 1/f Flicker Noise Reveal Differences in CFTR Substates.
papers.summary: Using time-frequency spectrograms and spectral analysis of single-channel CFTR recordings, the authors found 1/fα flicker noise with α=0.5 in the fully open state versus flat PSD in the closed state, distinct frequency and Hurst-exponent signatures for substates S1, S2 and F, and reproduced these findings with a transistor-based circuit model.

papers.title: Fast-Gelling, Adhesive, and Conductive Epidermal Electrode for Accurate Physiological Signal Monitoring and Real-Time Brain-Controlled Drone Flight.
papers.summary: The authors developed a fast-gelling (<5 min at room temperature) MXene/WPU/PAA conductive hydrogel epidermal electrode with strong adhesion and high conductivity, achieving sEMG and ECG signal-to-noise ratios of 36.0 dB and 30.1 dB that exceeded Ag/AgCl electrodes. The electrode also enabled scalp EEG monitoring that supported wireless drone flight control via real-time brainwave decoding.

papers.title: Maternal separation remodels Purkinje cell circuits and impairs cerebellar synaptic plasticity
papers.summary: In CD1 mice subjected to daily maternal separation from postnatal day 2 to 18, early-life stress produced cerebellar transcriptional remodeling, altered Purkinje cell dendritic arborization and excitatory inputs, impaired cerebellar long-term synaptic plasticity, glucocorticoid receptor promoter hypermethylation, and motor coordination, stress-coping, and social interaction deficits.

papers.title: Symptomatic plateau waves in a patient with leptomeningeal metastases captured with quantitative electroencephalography and intracranial pressure monitoring.
papers.summary: A case report describing symptomatic plateau waves in a patient with leptomeningeal metastases, captured using quantitative electroencephalography and intracranial pressure monitoring. It documents the simultaneous EEG and ICP correlates of these pressure waves in a neuro-oncology setting.

papers.title: Effect of neurofeedback-assisted mindfulness training on migraine severity, associated disability, sleep quality, and emotional distress: protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: A randomized controlled trial protocol testing a 12-week home-based neurofeedback-assisted mindfulness training program (Muse EEG headband) versus standard care in 66 adults with medium-to-high-frequency episodic migraine, with monthly migraine days as the primary outcome and secondary outcomes including disability, sleep, quality of life, and mood.

papers.title: Technology and Intelligence: Staying on Target for the Next Decade of Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: This perspective discusses technological and intelligence-related developments anticipated in cardiac electrophysiology over the next decade, with emphasis on arrhythmia mechanisms, mapping, ablation, and cardiac pacing.

papers.title: Side-to-side and other complex head movements as ictal signs in epilepsy: A video-EEG case series and review of literature.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: A video-EEG case series and literature review of 17 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy showing that ictal side-to-side and complex head movements occurred in focal seizures but had no localizing or lateralizing value, with heterogeneous presumed epileptogenic zones and likely reflecting seizure propagation.

papers.title: Imagery-based fear conditioning and extinction learning in individuals with psychotic liability: an EEG study.
papers.summary: A preregistered EEG study using imagery-based fear conditioning in individuals with psychotic liability (n=70 elevated psychosis proneness, n=28 clinical high-risk) versus controls (n=55), finding more pronounced acquisition in fear and arousal ratings and late positive potentials in the at-risk group and altered extinction learning.

papers.title: Potential Applications of Brain-Computer Interface Technology in the Rehabilitation of Patients with Anxiety Disorders: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: A narrative review examining the mechanistic rationale, technologies (EEG, fNIRS, rt-fMRI, invasive closed-loop), and integration of brain-computer interfaces in anxiety disorder rehabilitation, concluding that BCIs remain exploratory adjuncts limited by small single-center studies, heterogeneous protocols, and unresolved neural data governance.

papers.title: Visualization of super-selective Wada with computed tomography perfusion: toward a novel option in preoperative functional mapping.
papers.summary: Combined super-selective Wada test (ssWada) with CT perfusion (CTP) to visualize pharmacologically inactivated brain regions in 23 patients undergoing preoperative evaluation for brain tumors or drug-resistant epilepsy, and fused these data with MRI and post-SEEG CT. The approach enabled territory-based functional mapping with high spatial resolution; in the MCA superior trunk territory, repetition, naming, and reading tasks showed positive rates of approximately 70%, whereas in the inferior trunk territory, repetition and reading had high positive rates (93.8%) and naming positivity was lower (56.3%).

papers.title: A novel homozygous missense variant in the GAMT gene causing cerebral creatine deficiency syndrome 2 in an Iranian patient: molecular dynamics insights and literature review.
papers.summary: Reported a 17-year-old Iranian female with cerebral creatine deficiency syndrome 2 (CCDS2) carrying a novel homozygous GAMT missense variant (c.326A>G, p.Lys109Arg), classified as likely pathogenic. Molecular dynamics simulations over 100 ns showed that the substitution induced a more compact global conformation but drastically altered the dynamic coupling network, with a higher standard deviation in the cross-correlation matrix (0.323 vs. 0.236) and markedly increased numbers of strongly positive (4,006 vs. 1,574) and strongly negative (3,326 vs. 576) correlated residue pairs compared to wild-type.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
